summary: parkevtate Vosianc CFA's "Why Is Lowe's Stock Falling, and is it a Buying Opportunity?" (published 2026-09-30) is a dip-buy call: Lowe's (LOW, BUY at $189) with relatively HIGH conviction. His DCF fair value is $241, implying ~27% upside over 12–18 months. Beyond the call: the thesis is classic cyclical mean-reversion — revenue stagnated as pandemic-era demand was pulled forward (the 2020 home-improvement boom created a "reckoning" as repaint/remodel cycles stretched), compounded by shrinking disposable income (non-substitutable inflation in food, rent, insurance, healthcare) and management guiding flat-to-low-single-digit 2026 growth, with the stock down >20% in 2026 while the market rose double digits. The moat argument: home improvement is a ~$1T annual category that doesn't disappear — delayed projects eventually get done, and growth should re-accelerate to mid-to-high single digits once the economy normalizes. Margin pressure is the key risk: operating margin fell to 11.3% from over 15% in 2023, driven by wage inflation (McDonald's $20/hr California example feeding up the wage ladder); management's AI initiatives will improve profits only incrementally. Valuation hook: forward PE of 14.5, the lowest in several years. No other tickers called; Home Depot not mentioned. Sponsored by The Motley Fool.
